content:
Parents are being urged to reconsider limits on their children's screen time as the new school year begins. It has been suggested that stressed parents may have been more lenient with screen usage during the summer holidays, but this approach could have serious detrimental effects on children once the school term starts.

Additionally, experts have noted that the previously recommended two-hour daily limit is outdated, and parents should adopt a more nuanced approach based on the '5 Cs'...

CNET noted that parents face greater pressure when children are at home all day, making them more reliant on electronic devices to keep their kids occupied.

Experts say this may not necessarily be a problem.

However, if children fail to adjust after returning to school, they could be at risk.

Child development experts have pointed out that excessive use of digital media may lead to declining academic performance, impaired concentration, and reduced cognitive abilities.
